result.rationale:
The diff shows the zoho-bigin call site passes `credentialId` to refreshOAuthTokens (`"zoho-bigin",
 credentialId`) while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, lark, office365, msteams, webex, zohocrm, zoomvideo) passes `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint sends `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`, so in sharing mode Bigin would send a credential row id as the user id, breaking the documented sync contract.

judged_text: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId where every other call site passes credential.userId, so the sync endpoint receives the credential row id as calcomUserId. In sharing mode the parent app cannot map the request to a user (it gets a credential id, not the cal.com user id the sync contract documents), so Bigin token sync returns tokens for the wrong entity or none at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. But `refreshOAuthTokens`’s signature is `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and, in sharing mode, it sends that value as `calcomUserId` in the POST body (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). Other updated call sites consistently pass `credential.userId` (e.g. Hubspot/Lark/Office365/Zoom/Webex), so using a credential row id here would break the expected contract and prevent correct user mapping at the sync endpoint.
